clue.text: A heartless temperament in charge of the top room

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word with its heart cut out keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: only its first and last letters survive

explanation.surface: Someone with no warmth of character is given responsibility for the uppermost room of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room just under the roof, the highest in a house.

clue.text: Building in style of erect haircut

indicators.note: styling hair rearranges it, so these letters are restyled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be rearranged
taken as written, letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's description of a spiky upright cut, likened to a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture is the art and practice of designing and constructing buildings.

clue.text: Steam meat as stew for fellow players

indicators.note: a stew is a jumble of ingredients, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be stewed

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: steam the meat as a stew to feed the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Teammates are people who play together on the same side.

clue.text: Love amongst actors at the seaside

indicators.note: the love letter sits among the actors, inside the word for them

parts.note: the cast of a play is its actors
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A romance blooms among a touring company of actors playing a seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is the land beside the sea, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Send Mr Lynam with girl to Switzerland

parts.note: Des Lynam is a long-serving British sports television presenter
Pat is a girl's name
CH is Switzerland's international code, from Confoederatio Helvetica

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispatch the TV presenter and a young woman off to Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: Des Lynam fronted BBC sport for decades, so British solvers know him by first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To despatch something is to send it off, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Washing up liquid may put off old fashioned man!

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
gent is a dated word for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A joke that doing the dishes might discourage a traditional sort of man.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is the cleaning agent, such as washing-up liquid, used for dishes.

clue.text: Make catalogue

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a kind or type, as in a make of car
second meaning: to arrange or classify

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like verbs, but the first is the noun meaning a brand or kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a type or kind, and to sort is to classify items into order.

clue.text: Attacker found disguised as cruise worker

parts.note: taken as written
to cruise is to sail
a worker is a worker ant, the crossword's favourite insect

explanation.surface: A mugger has been unmasked, having posed as a member of a cruise ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found disguised' merely links: the attacker turns up spelt out by the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is someone who assaults or attacks another person.

clue.text: Ex-president drops on Mr Eastwood

indicators.note: the president's name lets fall the letters of the next word

parts.note: Bill Clinton was a former US president
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former president descends on the actor, as if dropping in on him.
explanation.definitionFit: Clint Eastwood is the American actor and director, so Clint is Mr Eastwood's first name.

clue.text: Distinguishing feature of the Arctic car is to break down!

indicators.note: a car breaking down suggests these letters falling apart and being reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters that break down

explanation.surface: A wry line that the defining trait of a car in the Arctic is that it breaks down.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic is a typical trait or quality that marks something out.

clue.text: Bystanders observe a variety of sweet sins

parts.note: to eye something is to watch or observe it

indicators.note: a variety means many forms, so these letters come in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be varied

explanation.surface: Onlookers watching a range of sugary indulgences at a sweet shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewitnesses are people who saw an event happen, like bystanders at a scene.

clue.text: I'm going to take friend around the old city green

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the friend goes around the old city, which ends up inside

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone planning to show a friend around a historic city that is green with parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes someone inexperienced or naive, which is what immature means.

clue.text: Squalid life goes round pointlessly and then you're old

indicators.note: the letters revolve into a new order
a point is a compass point, here east, which is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before losing its point
thy is the archaic form of your, a homophone-like pun on you're

explanation.surface: A grim reflection: squalid life passes in aimless circles and then you are old.
explanation.walkthrough: THY is the old form of 'your'; the clue writes 'you're', trading on the two sounding alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy means very dirty or squalid, a close synonym.

clue.text: Outgoing old lover gives a little tea to Trevor, who's upset

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: just a small piece of the word, its first letter

parts.note: only its first letter is used

indicators.note: Trevor's letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the name to be upset

explanation.surface: A sociable former partner offers a drop of tea to a distressed Trevor.
explanation.definitionFit: An extrovert is an outgoing, sociable person; here the adjective sense applies.

clue.text: Work ethic initially took a share in business

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: only the opening letter of ethic is used

parts.note: its first letter only
a ration is a fixed share or allowance

explanation.surface: Someone's work ethic first earned them a stake in a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work ethic' reads as one phrase, but Work is OP and ethic gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a business or enterprise, as in a small family operation.

clue.text: Counsellor takes the blame first

parts.note: taken as written
to take the rap is to take the blame
1st is written out as IST, with I for the digit one

explanation.surface: A counsellor who blames themselves before blaming the client.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 in 1ST becomes the letter I, a common trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist is a professional counsellor who treats mental or physical problems.

clue.text: A right quarrel leaves one in a quiver

parts.note: taken as written
a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: A proper argument leaves somebody trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiver' suggests trembling, but it is an archer's case for arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiver holds arrows, so an arrow is one item kept in it.

clue.text: Came in again to see tenant about point put to journalist

indicators.note: the journalist is attached at the end
the tenant goes about the point, which sits inside it

parts.note: a renter is someone who pays rent, a tenant
a compass point, east
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone returned to visit a tenant about a matter raised with a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to enter again, so re-entered means came in a second time.

clue.text: Try a bit of refinement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sample food, as a verb
second meaning: discernment in style and manners

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an invitation to be a little more refined; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste is to sample a morsel, and good taste is aesthetic discernment or refinement.

clue.text: Care for endless stream of people in races

indicators.note: the word loses both its ends

parts.note: only its middle letters survive

indicators.note: the people go inside the races

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
men are people

explanation.surface: Looking after a constant flow of racegoers or competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are motorbike races on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the care given to a patient, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cancel law about bell ringing

parts.note: a peal is a set of bells rung together

explanation.surface: Campaigners call for a noise statute about church bells to be scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal is to revoke or annul a law officially.

clue.text: Snap while making to hop

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be remade

explanation.surface: Something snaps while someone is trying to hop.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal word for a photograph, a quick snapshot.

clue.text: For example, eat half of butter spread on bread

indicators.note: spread suggests the letters are spread about and laid out afresh

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: half of keeps only the front three letters of the six-letter word butter

explanation.surface: An instruction to eat a slice of bread with some butter spread on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' butter gives BUT; EG, EAT and BUT are then mixed up, as 'spread' signals, to give the long French loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A baguette is a long thin French loaf, a type of bread.

clue.text: Don't start to mumble — articulate!

indicators.note: drop the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: to mutter is to speak low and indistinctly

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea to stop mumbling and speak clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say aloud, so it matches articulate as a verb of speaking.

clue.text: Stake placed by Mum's sister, they say

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: your mother's sister is your aunt

explanation.surface: A family member puts down money on a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match works where aunt is said like 'ant', as in much of England and North America.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a poker player's stake, put in before cards are dealt.

clue.text: Films action sketches

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: pictures that show motion

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a playful literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Motion pictures is a formal term for cinema films, and literally pictures in motion.

clue.text: The last born playing eagerly at first with toy guns

indicators.note: letters at play are moved about into a new order
only the first letter of eagerly

parts.note: its first letter only
taken as written, letters at play

explanation.surface: The baby of the family plays enthusiastically with toy guns.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest child is the one born last in a family.

clue.text: Travels in horrid estate car

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of horrid and the start of estate

explanation.surface: Someone gets about in a nasty old estate car.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British term for a station wagon; car only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel in or on a vehicle, so rides means travels.
